description: A from-scratch rich text editor control for WinUI 3, rendered with Win2D (CanvasVirtualControl / CanvasTextLayout). A port of AvaloniaRichEditor: text/paragraph formatting, tables (nested, colspan/rowspan, resize), inline & block images, hyperlinks, undo/redo, CJK/Korean IME, clipboard (rich/HTML/RTF), page view, print/PDF, find, and drop-in host controls. Byte-compatible .flow document format. Native AOT ready.
releaseNotes: See CHANGELOG.md. 1.1.1 exists because 1.1.0 shipped BROKEN UNDER NATIVE AOT. Win2D's CanvasTextLayout.LineMetrics returns a struct array that carries a bool, which CsWinRT cannot marshal ahead-of-time, and all eight callers fell back to "no lines": an AOT build could not move the caret vertically across a wrapped line, drew list bullets off the baseline, and measured every paragraph as a single line for pagination. It built, it ran and it rendered, so nothing looked wrong -- 1.1.0's own notes recorded the AOT publish as verified, because publishing and rendering was all that had been checked. JIT builds are unaffected: the API only fails ahead-of-time. NO API CHANGE AT ALL: the public surface is byte-identical to 1.1.0, so upgrading needs no code edits. Also fixed, from a 31-item external audit that was verified line by line against the code (11 confirmed, 4 disproven, 7 rejected, plus 2 the report missed): crashes in table column resize and TableBlock.Extract, an RTF tokenizer bug that could discard a whole document, Backspace/Delete/arrows splitting surrogate pairs, a right-click that did not see a picture inside a table cell, block/inline picture conversion doing nothing inside a cell (both directions), CSS percentage colours, and missing UIA text/selection notifications for screen readers. Memory: per-paragraph side caches no longer keep paragraphs that have left the document alive, and an undo checkpoint no longer allocates a table grid it discards (-40% on table-heavy documents). BEHAVIOUR: an over-wide RTF control-word parameter is no longer treated as damage, so RtfDocumentFormatter.TryParse accepts files it used to reject -- truncation, the damage files actually suffer, is still detected. Verification: 304 -> 391 tests, and a new harness that drives the same editing sequence through a JIT build and an AOT publish and compares both the faults reported and the resulting document; that comparison is what 1.1.0 was missing.
title: WinUIRichEditor
